inputs_summary.user_summary_sanitized: User owes back taxes for 2022-2023, received balance due notice, seeking payment plan guidance

assumptions: User's stated amount owed ($25,000) is accurate per IRS records
User has filed all required tax returns for 2022 and 2023
User does not have other outstanding IRS debts beyond stated amount
Standard IRS collection statute (10 years from assessment) applies
User qualifies for IRS standard allowable expense calculations

sources.title: Agreements for Payment of Tax Liability in Installments

outputs_summary.recommendation: Pursue streamlined installment agreement with 72-month term
outputs_summary.justification: Amount under $50k qualifies for streamlined IA with minimal financial disclosure; 72-month term provides affordable monthly payment

risks: Penalties and interest continue to accrue during payment plan (approximately 3-5% annually)
Missing a payment or owing new taxes can default the agreement, leading to IRS levy or lien
Payment plan may not be optimal; professional should evaluate Offer in Compromise eligibility
This analysis does NOT address potential penalty abatement (reasonable cause, first-time penalty abatement)
If user's actual monthly expenses exceed IRS allowable standards, may qualify for lower payment via non-streamlined IA
next_questions: Can you realistically afford $347/month payment for 6 years?
Do your actual monthly expenses exceed IRS allowable expense standards?
Should you pursue Offer in Compromise to settle for less than full amount?
Are you eligible for penalty abatement to reduce total owed?
Is the tax liability even correct? (Consider audit reconsideration if disputed)
